1 open issue - [Default missing usage details to zero during decoding](https://github.com/MacPaw/OpenAI/pull/483#discussion_r4488821032) · New
What changed in this PR This PR aims to preserve chat usage data when OpenAI-compatible providers omit prompt-token detail fields, without changing the public `Int` property types. **Changes:** - Adds custom decoding for prompt-token details using parsing options, shared by chat and streaming responses. - Adds a regression test for a response containing only `cached_tokens`, with relaxed parsing enabled. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | Tests/​OpenAITests/​ChatResultTests.swift | Tests usage decoding when `audio_tokens` is omitted. | | Sources/​OpenAI/​Public/​Models/​ChatResult.swift | Adds parsing-option-aware decoding for prompt-token details. |
Review effort: Balanced

review_comments.body: Declaring `init(from:)` in the struct body stops Swift from synthesizing the memberwise `init(audioTokens:cachedTokens:)`, so `PromptTokensDetails` can now only be created by decoding, even from `@testable` tests. Could you either move `init(from:)` into an extension, or add a `public init(audioTokens:cachedTokens:)` like `CompletionTokensDetails` has? A public one would also make the `promptTokensDetails:` parameter of `CompletionUsage.init` usable for anyone mocking usage.

With the default parsing options (`[]`), `decodeInt` still throws when either detail is missing, so both `ChatResult` and `ChatStreamResult` discard the entire `usage`. Use `decodeIfPresent(Int.self, forKey:) ?? 0` for both fields so default-configured clients receive the intended fallback. Remove the `.relaxed` setting in `Tests/OpenAITests/ChatResultTests.swift:239` so the regression test covers that default behavior.
@pcbeingused333 forget it, I'll just resolve it. Claude wanted the same thing. Agents don't understand what strict mode means.
